You are synthesizing a unified hypothesis from multiple parent hypotheses.
Goal: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from the limitation group 'Leakage-free generalisation protocol': L1, L2, L11, L20, L22, L27, L37, C2): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and with a simple supervised baseline trained on the same labelled images (L31) where relevant.
Parent hypotheses: Parent 1:
TITLE: Cross-level consensus MIL: choosing instances by agreement of the four adapter levels
SUMMARY: Select the positive instances of an abnormal image as the patches on which all four segmentation levels agree (geometric mean of level probabilities) and apply the MIL loss to those patches at every level, in a single training stage.
HYPOTHESIS: Training MVFA's segmentation adapters with consensus MIL — top-k (k = 1%) selected on the geometric mean of the four level maps rather than per level — raises held-out pixel AUROC by at least 2 points and AUPRO by at least 3 points over per-level top-k MIL, because single-level top-k selections disagree and each level reinforces its own spurious maxima.
RATIONALE: The self-distillation parent shows that cross-level agreement filters noisy evidence, but uses it only after training, in a second stage that can lock in errors. The anchor-frame parent shows that all four levels read their patches in the same fixed anchor frame, so their probabilities are directly comparable across levels. Together they suggest a different mechanism: use cross-level agreement inside the MIL loss itself, as the instance selector. Per-level top-k lets each level pick its own (often anatomical) maxima; a consensus selector picks only patches that every level finds anomalous, which are more likely to be lesions, and then trains every level on those patches. This is one-stage, needs no pseudo-masks, and is a direct modification of the problem's operator.
METHOD: 1) loss.py: consensus_mil(p_levels, label, k_frac=0.01): c = exp(mean_l log p_l) per patch; idx = topk(c); positive loss for abnormal images = mean over levels of BCE(mean(p_l[idx]), 1); normal images: BCE(top-k mean of p_l, 0) per level as in the problem. 2) train_zero.py: replace the problem's per-level top-k MIL with consensus_mil; selection indices are detached. 3) Hyper-parameters: k_frac {0.5%, 1%, 2%}; consensus by geometric mean (ablation: minimum over levels); released learning rate and epochs. 4) Inference unchanged.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Ablations: geometric mean vs. minimum; consensus over levels 2-4 only. Diagnostics: overlap of per-level top-k selections; fraction of selected patches inside true masks on masked source images. Falsified if consensus MIL does not beat per-level MIL in AUPRO.

Parent 2:
TITLE: Is it the words or the frame? Anchor controls for MIL-trained segmentation adapters
SUMMARY: Train the segmentation adapters with the problem's top-k MIL against three references — MVFA's text anchors, scale-matched random anchors, and a learned linear patch head — and test which property (meaning, fixed frame, scale) drives transfer of weakly supervised localisation.
HYPOTHESIS: Under top-k MIL, scale-matched random anchors reach held-out pixel AUROC within 1 point of MVFA's text anchors, while breaking the scale match (0.5x, 2x) reduces it by at least 2 points, and the learned linear head transfers worse than any fixed frame.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: patch-scoring reference during MIL training and testing (text anchors; random anchor pair with the same difference-vector length; random pair with 0.5x and 2x length; learned linear head, i.e. a learnable difference vector). Dependent variables: held-out pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC; plus the same comparison with mask supervision, so the effect of weak supervision and of the reference can be separated.
RATIONALE: The problem's hypothesis credits transfer of MIL-learned localisation to text anchors shared by all modalities. Do Words Matter? predicts that what is shared is a fixed coordinate frame and its scale, not linguistic content. This makes the hypothesis sharper and testable: if transfer comes from a fixed frame, scale-matched random anchors should localise as well as text anchors under MIL, and a per-modality learned head (no shared frame) should transfer worse.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: make_anchors(kind, seed): text (as released), random (Gaussian, normalised, difference rescaled to the text pair's difference length), scaled variants. 2) loss.py: topk_mil as in the problem. 3) train_zero.py: flag --anchors {text, rand, rand05, rand2, learned}; for 'learned' a 768-d difference vector is an nn.Parameter initialised to the text difference. 4) test_zero.py uses the same anchors as training. 5) Hyper-parameters as released; 3 random-anchor draws per seed.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA with text anchors and with scale-matched random anchors. Falsified if random anchors lose more than 2 points to text anchors under MIL (meaning matters) or if the learned head transfers as well as the fixed frames (frame does not matter).
